title: Data of a simultaneous local resolution invariant calculus
statement:
For raw histories, their smooth and intrinsic comparisons, and admissibility relative to a simultaneous value assignment [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history], let $V$ be a totally ordered set with least element $ ot$. A resolution invariant calculus consists of one simultaneous family $
u_H:|X_H|	o V$ satisfying the following conditions on its admissible histories. Each image is finite, and $
u_H(x)= ot$ exactly when the local ring at $x$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Every nonregular $X_H$ has an extension at the reduced full positive maximum locus. Every such center is nonempty, regular, nowhere dense in $X_H$, and its ideals on $X_H$ and the ambient scheme are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. After this extension the ambient scheme is again smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], its strict transform is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and its next positive maximum is strictly smaller. Every smooth ambient pullback of an admissible history exists with exactly its empty-center stages deleted, and values agree at corresponding points, with no relative-dimension restriction. A reduced stratum ideal is an ideal cutting out the equality locus $
u_H=a$ whose closed subscheme is reduced. Reduced maximum-stratum ideals extend under smooth comparison to the reduced inverse-image-stratum ideals, with the unit ideal in the empty case. Intrinsic comparisons of two admissible histories identify their values and all reduced maximum-stratum ideals; these comparisons use actual point maps and ideal extensions, so are compatible with restriction and further pullback. For every initial pair there is no infinite chain of successive maximum extensions starting at an empty history. This termination condition concerns this family and does not impose well-foundedness on $V$. All embedded pairs are included, including empty schemes and finite disjoint unions of components of different dimensions. This defines data and conditions only; existence is a separate theorem.
